- [JavaScript API](docs/javascript-api.md) — next on the reading path, for programmatic CSS or SVG generation.

<!-- Source: docs/javascript-api.md -->

# JavaScript API

The Tailwind, Vite, and PostCSS plugins are thin wrappers around a small set of exported helpers. Reach for these functions directly when you generate CSS or SVG outside a bundler, load icon families lazily at runtime, animate icons from application events, or wire up a pre-configured `IconRegistry` for a plugin to reuse.

```ts
import { generateIconSetCss, getIconCssProps, IconRegistry, renderSvg } from "@codenhub/icons";
import lucide from "@codenhub/icons/data/lucide";

const registry = new IconRegistry({ defaultPrefix: "lucide" });
registry.registerFamily(lucide);

const heart = registry.resolve("lucide:heart");
renderSvg(heart!, { strokeWidth: 1.5 });

const { css, families } = generateIconSetCss(["ic-lucide-heart", "ic-lucide-heart/1.5"], registry);

getIconCssProps("lucide:x", registry);
// { "--ic-uri": 'url("data:image/svg+xml;…")', "--ic-mask": "var(--ic-uri)" }
```

`generateIconSetCss` returns both the generated CSS and the list of `families` it drew from, so a caller knows which license notices belong in the banner. Every export and option is documented in the [API reference](docs/reference/index.md).

## Generating CSS outside a bundler

At bottom, every plugin just runs a scan followed by a CSS emit. You can run the exact same two-step pipeline yourself in a build script or static generator:

```ts
import { generateIconSetCss, IconRegistry, renderAttributionBanner, scanFiles } from "@codenhub/icons";
import lucide from "@codenhub/icons/data/lucide";

const registry = new IconRegistry({ defaultPrefix: "lucide" });
registry.registerFamily(lucide);

const classes = scanFiles(["./src/**/*.html"]);
const { css, families } = generateIconSetCss(classes, registry);
const banner = renderAttributionBanner(families); // undefined when no family used has a notice line to print
const stylesheet = banner ? `${banner}\n${css}` : css;
```

`scanFiles` accepts literal file paths and glob patterns, and quietly skips any file it cannot read rather than blowing up your script over a stray permission error.

If you want one full family stylesheet — the same format `@codenhub/icons/<family>` ships — call `generateFamilyCss`. For a brand family, pass `bareNames: false`, as its published stylesheet does, so a brand named like a core icon never claims that icon's bare class. Both CSS generators emit a `--ic-static-mask` property for the base stylesheet to swap in on hover rest and under reduced motion whenever an icon provides `staticBody`; the registry preserves that optional inner SVG markup on `ResolvedIcon`. It shares the animated body's geometry and accepts the same stroke width. `renderSvg`, by contrast, keeps the animated `body`. See [Animated families](docs/concepts.md#animated-families).

## A background-image icon

The base stylesheet styles icons on an element (`<i>` or `.ic`) or an inlined `<svg>`. When CSS puts the icon in a place with no inner element — a custom form control, an input affix, or a `::before` pseudo-element you own — resolve the `url()` in JavaScript and feed it to your CSS yourself:

```ts
getIconMaskUrl("lucide:search", registry); // 'url("data:image/svg+xml;…")'
getIconCssProps("lucide:search", registry); // { "--ic-uri": …, "--ic-mask": "var(--ic-uri)" }
```

`getIconMaskUrl` also accepts a raw string starting with `<svg` and encodes it directly without consulting a registry — pass the element markup itself, with no leading whitespace or XML declaration. `getIconCssProps` includes `--ic-static-mask` when the resolved icon supplies static artwork, which the base stylesheet uses for reduced motion and hover rest. It returns the exact custom-property object an inline `style` attribute or CSS-in-JS object expects; pair those properties with `background-image: var(--ic-uri)` or `mask-image: var(--ic-mask)` and your own sizing.

## Playing icons from code

`@codenhub/icons/play` is an opt-in entry point for playback behavior CSS cannot handle on its own. It loads no icon data, and simply importing it does nothing until you call one of its two functions:

```ts
import { bindIconPlayback, playIcon } from "@codenhub/icons/play";

// Replay one-shot artwork on every hover, not only the first:
const unbind = bindIconPlayback();

// Play an icon on an event, such as a successful copy:
copyButton.addEventListener("click", async () => {
  await navigator.clipboard.writeText(value);
  playIcon(copyButton.querySelector(".ic-anim-beat")!);
});

// When the page or component is disposed:
unbind();
```

`playIcon(element, { prefix: "ic" })` restarts an icon from frame zero, whether it uses an `ic-anim-*` class (running or finished) or animated SVG artwork. For glyph motion, it briefly clears `animation-name` for one style recalculation and restores it. For a CSS-mask icon, it writes a fresh SVG data URL to the inline `--ic-mask` property, because browsers refuse to restart an animated mask image they have already painted once. A direct call leaves that inline override on the element, so clear it with `element.style.removeProperty("--ic-mask")` before swapping the icon class later. Inline `<svg>` icons restart via `setCurrentTime(0)`. An element with neither kind of motion is left untouched.

`bindIconPlayback(root = document, { prefix: "ic" })` calls `playIcon` for every `ic-on-hover` icon when its trigger activates, following the exact same trigger rule as the CSS: the icon itself, its parent, or any `ic-trigger` ancestor on hover or `:focus-visible`. CSS alone already restarts glyph motion and looping artwork on every hover; this binder is what lets one-shot artwork, such as a Line MD draw-in, replay on every hover instead of only the first. It attaches delegated listeners, so icons mounted later work automatically. Pass a subtree containing both the triggers and their icons to scope it. Moving the pointer between children inside the same trigger preserves the active playback, and when the trigger ends, the binder cleans up its inline `--ic-mask` override so future icon-class changes work normally. Calling the returned cleanup function removes the listeners and clears active overrides.

Passing a custom `prefix` shifts the classes, custom property, and animation names both functions target. Both functions do nothing when the device requests reduced motion: CSS-mask icons keep their static fallback, while inline SVG keeps its own animated artwork, so substitute static artwork yourself when needed. Calling `bindIconPlayback` with no `root` outside a browser returns a no-op cleanup function. Chrome playback is verified; Firefox and Safari are untested. See [Motion](docs/concepts.md#motion) for the CSS controls.

## Loading a family on demand

In a browser UI such as an icon picker, bundling every family up front would weigh megabytes. Register async loaders instead so families load only when someone asks for them:

```ts
registry.registerLoader("phosphor", () => import("@codenhub/icons/data/phosphor"));

await registry.resolveAsync("phosphor:heart");
```

`resolve` stays synchronous and checks only families already in memory, whereas `resolveAsync` loads the requested family first. Build-time plugins stay on the synchronous path because a build knows its configured families before it starts scanning.

## Third-party icon sets

`adoptIconifySet` converts an IconifyJSON document into the family format this package expects. It reads the icons, aliases, and their dimensions, plus the set's name, author, and license; other IconifyJSON fields, such as categories, are not carried over:

```ts
import { adoptIconifySet } from "@codenhub/icons";

registry.registerFamily(adoptIconifySet(someIconifySet, { attribution: "notice" }));
```

Pass `attribution: "credit"` instead when the adopted set's license requires visible authorship credit, such as CC-BY.

Adopted sets belong to the `extended` tier: the licensing promise this package makes covers the families it generates, not data a consumer supplies. See [Licensing](docs/licensing.md).

## Next

Read [Licensing](docs/licensing.md) to see what attribution your build emits for each delivery method and what obligations apply to core, brand, and adopted icon sets.

<!-- Source: docs/licensing.md -->

# Licensing and attribution

This page explains what your build owes for the icon artwork it ships, how the `attribution` option works, how each delivery method carries the required notice, and what trademark constraints apply to brand icons.

Every bundled, generated family ships the license text and attribution notice its artwork requires; those files travel with the package regardless of what a build outputs. A third-party set adopted through `adoptIconifySet` is not covered by that guarantee — supply its license and attribution material yourself.

## Attribution modes

The `attribution` option controls how license notices reach your build output:

| Mode             | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `auto` (default) | Prepends a `/*! … */` banner to the generated CSS, naming only the families the build used. Vite's inline SVG mode, which has no stylesheet, emits `icons-attribution.txt` instead. |
| `file`           | Emits `icons-attribution.txt` as a build asset instead. Vite only.                                                                                                                  |
| `off`            | Emits nothing, and warns when a family used still requires a notice.                                                                                                                |

## How the notice travels

Each delivery method carries the notice through a mechanism that its pipeline supports:

| Method             | How the notice travels                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Vite               | A `/*! … */` banner on the generated CSS, or `icons-attribution.txt` under `file` and in inline SVG mode. |
| PostCSS            | A `/*! … */` banner on the generated CSS.                                                                 |
| Tailwind `/tw`     | A `/*! … */` banner opening `dist/tw/index.css`, naming every family it resolves.                         |
| Tailwind `@plugin` | A `--ic-attribution-<family>` custom property on `:root`, one per family the build used.                  |
| Plain CSS          | A `/*! … */` banner opening each family stylesheet you imported.                                          |

`@import "@codenhub/icons/tw"` inlines a static file, so it carries an ordinary `/*! … */` banner. Because that file makes every bundled family resolvable except brand families, the banner names all of those core families — a superset notice, which satisfies the license requirement safely. Declaring the plugin yourself with `@plugin "@codenhub/icons/tailwind"` narrows resolution, and there the notice is emitted as a `--ic-attribution-<family>` custom property instead: Tailwind's plugin API generates CSS declarations rather than comments, and the property is emitted the first time a family produces a utility, so the output carries notices only for the artwork it actually shipped.

## Obligation levels

Permissive licenses still carry different distribution requirements, grouped into three levels:

- **`none`** — public-domain dedications. Nothing is owed in distributed output.
- **`notice`** — MIT, ISC, and Apache-2.0. The copyright and license notice must accompany distributed output, which `auto` and `file` handle automatically.
- **`credit`** — CC-BY and similar licenses. The author must be credited visibly.

Every bundled family except `simple-icons` and `logos` belongs to the `core` tier, meaning its obligation level is `none` or `notice`, so a default build satisfies its license terms automatically. Note that a minifier configured with `legalComments: "none"` strips CSS comments, including `/*! … */` banners; use `attribution: "file"` in Vite, or preserve legal comments in your minifier config.

A set adopted through `adoptIconifySet` belongs to the `extended` tier — you remain responsible for complying with its license terms and providing its attribution material. See [JavaScript API](docs/javascript-api.md).

## Brand families

`simple-icons` and `logos` belong to the `brand` tier: one-color logos from [Simple Icons](https://simpleicons.org) and full-color logos from [gilbarbara/logos](https://github.com/gilbarbara/logos), both dedicated to the public domain under CC0. Neither family owes a license notice, but a logo is a trademark, and the trademark is separate from the copyright license: using a mark remains subject to its owner's brand guidelines, which no build option can satisfy or verify.

- **Opt-in only.** Vite and PostCSS load only the families you pass. `@codenhub/icons/tw` never resolves brand families; a declared `@plugin "@codenhub/icons/tailwind"` resolves them only when its `families` option names them.
- **Trademark notice line.** Each family's notice line, wherever the build emits one, states that the marks are trademarks of their owners. Setting `attribution: "off"` suppresses it without a warning because no license requires it.
- **Excluded Simple Icons entries.** Simple Icons records a separate license for some icons. Icons whose own license adds any obligation are excluded, so no icon in the family carries a recorded license obligation: each is CC0, Unlicense, or has no license recorded upstream.
- **Recoloring and guidelines.** Each brand icon renders in its brand colors by default, and `--ic-color` can recolor it; a full-color logo becomes a monochrome silhouette. Owners' guidelines commonly permit a mark in its official colors or plain monochrome and restrict arbitrary colors; check the owner's terms when recoloring a mark. See [Color](docs/concepts.md#color).
- **Simple Icons removals.** Simple Icons removes icons when brand owners request it. Upgrading the package across an upstream major version can remove icon names; check the changelog for removed names.
- **Pinned `logos` source.** gilbarbara/logos publishes no releases, so `logos` is generated from a pinned commit, and upgrading it can remove or rename logos; check the changelog for changes. A few upstream files whose markup cannot render as a self-contained icon, such as files embedding a bitmap, are excluded, and the family's `ATTRIBUTION.md` lists them.

## Next

Read [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) if an icon fails to appear, renders as a solid square, ignores stroke width, or drops its license notice.

<!-- Source: docs/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting

Most icon failures are silent: the build succeeds and the missing or broken icon shows up only in the browser. Jump to the symptom that matches what you see.

## The icon renders as nothing

No base rule matched the element, so it has no size — or, in inline SVG mode, no SVG replaced it or an ID collision hid it.

- **No base rules.** Plain CSS and a declared Tailwind `@plugin` need `@import "@codenhub/icons";` in a stylesheet. `@codenhub/icons/tw`, the Vite plugin's stylesheet, and the PostCSS plugin include the base rules already (for PostCSS, unless `injectBase` is `false`). Inline SVG mode renders without base rules, though adding `@import "@codenhub/icons"` supplies `--ic-size`, the size classes, and `--ic-color` for icons without a color of their own.
- **The element is not an `<i>` and has no `.ic`.** The base rules match `<i class="ic-…">`, or any element that also carries `.ic`. A `<span class="ic-lucide-heart">` without `.ic` matches neither.
- **An inlined logo whose first copy is hidden.** In inline SVG mode, two copies of the same `logos` icon share gradient, mask, and clip-path ids. If the first copy sits inside a `display: none` element, every later copy renders blank (seen in Chromium). Move a visible copy ahead of the hidden one, hide with `visibility: hidden`, or use CSS mode; see [Vite § Inline SVG mode](docs/delivery/vite.md#inline-svg-mode).

## The icon renders as a solid square

The base rules sized and colored the element, so it appears as a box — but no mask rule matched it, leaving the entire box painted in the icon color.

- **The name does not exist in the family.** Names are upstream names: Material Symbols writes `check_circle`, Lucide writes `circle-check`, and Lucide has no `close` (it is `x`). Check the exact name in the family; see [Finding an icon's name](docs/concepts.md#finding-an-icons-name).
- **An unqualified name with no default family.** `ic-heart` resolves only where you set a default: `defaultPrefix` in the Vite and PostCSS plugins, `default:` in the Tailwind plugin, or the last core family stylesheet imported in plain CSS. Write the qualified `ic-lucide-heart`, or configure a default. See [Names](docs/concepts.md#names).
- **The family is not loaded.** The Vite and PostCSS plugins resolve only the families listed in `families`, or registered in the `registry` passed in its place.
- **A brand icon through `@codenhub/icons/tw`.** `/tw` never resolves `simple-icons` or `logos`. Declare the plugin with `families` naming the brand family; see [Tailwind CSS](docs/delivery/tailwind.md#configuring-the-plugin).
- **The class is assembled at runtime.** Build plugins find a class only when it is written out in full: `` `ic-${name}` `` is invisible at build time. Write each class literally, or load the icon as a [module](docs/delivery/vite.md#one-module-per-icon).
- **The class is in a file the plugin does not scan.** The Vite plugin scans the modules Vite transforms; a file it never transforms needs a `content` glob, and so do Astro and SvelteKit builds, where the stylesheet can be generated before every module is transformed. The PostCSS plugin scans only the stylesheet itself and `content`. See [Vite § Scanning](docs/delivery/vite.md#scanning) and [PostCSS § Scanning](docs/delivery/postcss.md#scanning).
- **Astro, production build only.** Production `astro build` skips Vite's HTML hook, so import `virtual:icons.css` explicitly from a shared layout. See [Astro § Vite plugin](docs/frameworks/astro.md#vite-plugin).
- **Production only, with a Content Security Policy.** Versions up to 0.2.1 inlined the built stylesheet as a `<style>` tag, which a policy without `'unsafe-inline'` blocks. Upgrade past 0.2.1 so CSS-mode builds with HTML entries link a stylesheet asset instead; library builds and inline SVG mode emit no stylesheet at all; see [Vite § Scanning](docs/delivery/vite.md#scanning).
- **Inline SVG mode, on an element it does not rewrite.** `mode: "svg"` replaces `<i class="ic-…">` tags and emits no mask rules, so `.ic` on any other element has no rule behind it. The build warns, naming the class and the file. Under Astro, `.md` and `.mdx` are not rewritten and nothing warns; wrap the icon in a component for `.mdx`, or use CSS mode for `.md`. See [Vite § Inline SVG mode](docs/delivery/vite.md#inline-svg-mode) and [Astro § Inline SVG mode](docs/frameworks/astro.md#inline-svg-mode).

## The stroke width does not change

- **Plain CSS.** Family stylesheets carry each icon at its authored width; `ic-lucide-heart/1.5` needs Tailwind, Vite, or PostCSS. See [Stroke width](docs/concepts.md#stroke-width).
- **A family drawn with fills.** Only `lucide` and `line-md` are stroke-based. Every other bundled family ignores the modifier.

## The color does not change

Set `--ic-color` on the icon or an ancestor, or `--<prefix>-color` under a custom class prefix. Plain `color` reaches only icons without a color of their own: a brand icon keeps its brand color until `--ic-color` overrides it. Setting `background-color` on the icon element itself replaces its paint, because CSS mask icons paint through their `background`. In inline SVG mode under a Content Security Policy that blocks `style` attributes, a brand icon keeps its brand color and ignores `--ic-color`. See [Color](docs/concepts.md#color).

## A brand icon is invisible in dark mode

Its brand color is near-black, as GitHub's, X's, and Vercel's are. Set `--ic-color` to a light color on those classes inside your dark theme. See [Color](docs/concepts.md#color).

## The license notice is missing from the output

A minifier configured with `legalComments: "none"` strips `/*! … */` comments. Use `attribution: "file"` with Vite to emit `icons-attribution.txt`, or configure your minifier to keep legal comments. See [Licensing](docs/licensing.md).

## Next

Return to the [Overview](docs/index.md) for the full reading path, or look up individual exports and options in the [API reference](docs/reference/index.md).

<!-- Source: docs/changelog/0.4.0.md -->

# 0.4.0

## Added

- Motion classes that move the whole icon: `ic-anim-spin`, `ic-anim-pulse`, `ic-anim-beat`, `ic-anim-bounce`, and `ic-anim-wiggle`. They run for as long as the class is present, `--ic-anim-duration` sets their speed, `--ic-anim-iterations` their repeat count, and `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` turns them off. In Tailwind they are utilities, so variants such as `group-hover:ic-anim-spin` work too. They move the whole glyph: the artwork is a CSS mask, so parts of an icon cannot be animated from the page. See Concepts, Motion.
- `ic-on-hover` plays an icon's motion, from a motion class or from its animated artwork, while its trigger is hovered or has visible focus, and holds it at rest otherwise: upright, or on its static artwork. The trigger is the icon, its parent, or any ancestor marked `ic-trigger`, such as a card. Each hover plays from the start, once by default; `--ic-anim-iterations: infinite` keeps it moving while hovered.
- `@codenhub/icons/play`, an opt-in entry point with no icon data. `playIcon(element)` plays an icon from the start, for feedback on an event such as a copy or a like. `bindIconPlayback()` replays one-shot artwork, such as a Line MD draw-in, on every hover rather than the first only, which CSS cannot do because a browser does not restart an image it has already shown. See JavaScript API, Playing icons from code.
- `line-md`, a core family of 1,222 animated, stroke-based icons such as `ic-line-md-loading-loop` and `ic-line-md-heart`, from [Line MD](https://github.com/cyberalien/line-md) 3.0.5 under MIT, and its stylesheet `@codenhub/icons/line-md`. Icons named `-loop` animate continuously; the others draw in or morph once. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, CSS masks switch to the upstream static artwork, in the family stylesheet, Tailwind, and CSS mode in Vite and PostCSS; inline SVG keeps the animated artwork, since CSS cannot stop it. Tested in Chrome only; Firefox and Safari are untested. See Concepts, Animated families.
- `svg-spinners`, a core family of 46 loading indicators such as `ic-svg-spinners-90-ring`, from [SVG Spinners](https://github.com/n3r4zzurr0/svg-spinners) under MIT, and its stylesheet `@codenhub/icons/svg-spinners`. They keep animating under reduced motion, because the motion conveys loading.
- `--ic-static-mask` carries an animated icon's static artwork, next to `--ic-mask`. `IconData.staticBody` and `ResolvedIcon.staticBody` carry the same artwork as markup.
- `chi build`, a command that reads a project's files and writes a stylesheet holding the base rules and only the icons they use, for a project that runs neither Tailwind CSS, Vite, nor PostCSS. Its options are the PostCSS plugin's, and it writes the same rules, stroke-width modifiers such as `ic-lucide-heart/1.5` included. It resolves every family except the brand ones unless `--family` names others, fails without writing when a `--content` glob matches no file, and warns once on the classes that resolve to no icon. Run it from a `package.json` script, or as `npx @codenhub/icons build`. See Delivery methods, Build command.

## Changed

- **Breaking.** The `<svg>` a `virtual:@codenhub/icons/<family>/<name>` module exports carries the icon's qualified class, such as `class="ic-lucide-tag"`, so the base rules size and color it from `--ic-size`, `--ic-color`, and the `ic-xs`–`ic-xl` classes, as they do an `<svg>` that svg mode inlines. Code that adds its own `class` attribute to that markup as a string now produces a second one; add to the existing attribute, or use `classList`. [codenhub/codenhub#452](https://github.com/codenhub/codenhub/issues/452)
- **Breaking.** `anim` is reserved for the motion utilities, as `xs`–`xl` are for size. A class `ic-anim` or `ic-anim-*` never resolves as an icon, including from a family adopted with `adoptIconifySet`, and the generator refuses a family prefix or icon named that way, or leaves the icon out of a brand family. The exact names `on-hover` and `trigger` are reserved the same way. No icon in a shipped family is affected.
- **Breaking.** A relative `content` entry for the Vite plugin is read from Vite's `root` instead of the working directory, so `./src/**/*.astro` finds the app's files when the build runs from a monorepo root or with `vite --root`. A project whose `root` differs from the directory it builds from and whose entries were written relative to that directory needs them rewritten relative to `root`, or made absolute. The PostCSS plugin, which has no root, still reads from the working directory.
- **Breaking.** Node.js 26 or newer. `engines.node` is `>=26`, so Yarn 1, and npm with `engine-strict`, refuse the install on Node.js 24. Update Node.js where the package is installed or where the build-time plugins and helpers run; the plain CSS stylesheets themselves need nothing. See [Overview → Requirements](docs/index.md#requirements). ([#553](https://github.com/codenhub/codenhub/issues/553))
- The package is larger: the tarball unpacks to about 72 MB, up from 67 MB, and the full `line-md` stylesheet is about 3 MB, a third of it the static fallback. CSS from the plugins still carries only the icons a project uses.

## Fixed

- In `mode: "svg"`, an icon tag written inside a string in an `.astro` frontmatter broke `astro build` with a parse error. Astro compiled the file before the plugin's transform ran, so the `<svg>` landed unescaped in a string the compiler had re-quoted. The transform now runs ahead of other plugins' ordinary transforms, Astro's compiler among them; a plugin that also orders its transform `"pre"` and is listed earlier still runs first. [codenhub/codenhub#451](https://github.com/codenhub/codenhub/issues/451)
- In `mode: "svg"`, an icon inlined as a React JSX element kept HTML attribute names such as `stroke-width`, so React logged an invalid DOM property warning for every stroked icon in development. In a project that uses `@vitejs/plugin-react` or `@vitejs/plugin-react-swc`, hyphenated attributes in a JSX element are now written as React names them, such as `strokeWidth` and `fillRule`, and a `style` becomes an object. Solid, Preact, and Vue JSX write attribute names into HTML as given, so there the hyphenated names and the `style` string stay. An icon tag inside a string, as one assigned to `innerHTML`, keeps the hyphenated names the HTML parser reads. [codenhub/codenhub#561](https://github.com/codenhub/codenhub/issues/561)
- In `mode: "svg"`, a quote in JSX text, such as the apostrophe in `<p>Don't</p>`, made the transform treat the next icon tag as part of a string and escape its markup, so the page showed the escaped `<svg>`. A string now ends at its line, and a quote opens one only where an expression can start.
- In `mode: "svg"`, an icon tag with a `>` inside an attribute, such as `onClick={() => a > b}` or `title="a > b"`, was cut at that `>` and left broken markup. The whole tag is now replaced.
- In `mode: "svg"`, a file with many unclosed `<i` tags took over a minute to transform. It now takes milliseconds.
- In `mode: "svg"`, a quote in a `.vue` or `.svelte` template, which the framework reads as markup, made the next icon inlined inside it be escaped as if it were in a JavaScript string. Templates and `<script>` blocks are now read separately.
- In `mode: "svg"`, an icon removed from a file kept its family in the attribution notice, and its class in the unresolved-class warning, of every later build in the same process, such as `vite build --watch`. Each file now forgets what it used when it is transformed again or deleted.
- With the Tailwind plugin, a variant on a motion utility, such as `hover:ic-anim-spin`, lost its animation in a production build, because Tailwind's optimizer drops a rule that nests `@keyframes`. The keyframes are now declared once at the top level.
- `playIcon` and `bindIconPlayback` threw in jsdom, which has neither `matchMedia` nor `SVGSVGElement.setCurrentTime`. Without `matchMedia`, an icon is not played, since the page cannot say whether motion is reduced; an inline `<svg>` without `setCurrentTime` restarts its glyph motion only.
- `generateFamilyCss` with `bareNames` wrote a bare selector for an icon named like a motion utility, such as `anim-spin`, so `class="ic-anim-spin"` painted that icon. Such an icon now keeps only its qualified selector.
- An `ic-on-hover` icon that itself had keyboard focus stayed at rest, though its focused parent or `ic-trigger` played it. The icon now plays when it has `:focus-visible` too, in CSS as `bindIconPlayback` already did.
- An icon name inherited by every JavaScript object, such as `ic-lucide-constructor`, resolved as an empty icon. Only a family's own icons and aliases resolve now.
